youtube.title: GIGI FOSTER
youtube.summary: Economist and freedom advocate Gigi Foster returns for a discussion with Paul about the multi-various legislative threats to free speech in Australia and how people are slowly beginning to push back. Discover more from Australians for Science and Freedom

youtube.title: SHUBZ
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with Shubz from Iwi Fakamahu – Heal the Nation, on a pop-up tour through New Zealand, sharing stories of healing, unity, and personal growth. Shubz reflects on the physical toll of the journey, the powerful stories being shared, and why his focus remains on healing rather than politics. He addresses public allegations, explains the significance of travelling to Waitangi, and invites people of all backgrounds to walk together in kotahitanga, connection, and simple human kindness. You can follow Heal The Nation – Iwi Whakamahu on Facebook or support the tour through Give A Little You can find Shubz on X

youtube.title: TREVOR LOUDON
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by political researcher and author Trevor Loudon for an in-depth discussion on global geopolitical shifts, communist influence across multiple countries, and what this means for upcoming elections. They explore developments in Venezuela, Iran, Greenland, and the United States, including internal political dynamics and voter vigilance, with a particular focus on the implications for New Zealand. For more information visit Trevor's website or find him on Keykiwi To Purchase Trevor Loudon's books

youtube.title: GREENWASHED
youtube.summary: Jaspreet Boparai and Don Nicolson examine claims the United Nations is heading for a financial crunch, questioning how an organisation that took in more than US$60 billion in 2023 can be “running out of money”. They trace how New Zealand’s UN contributions jumped from about US$15 million in 2016 to nearly US$70 million by 2023, then widen the lens to global tax cooperation plans, Agenda 2030, and climate-linked funding. The discussion raises concerns about transparency, sovereignty, and whether New Zealand is getting value for money. For more information: Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee on the United Nations Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation underway in NY currently The terms of reference of the Committee that refers “developing a framework convention will also help in accelerating the implementation of the Addis Ababa Action Agenda on Financing for Development and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. & “Tax cooperation on environmental challenges” Shane Reti reaffirming the SGs at Spain in 2025 One News: UN claiming $$ crunch The UN- FTS (Financial Tracking Service ) to scroll through our UN – funding year on year The Addis Ababa Agenda Circa 20

youtube.title: PAUL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan kicks off 2026’s first mailbag with strong reactions to past interviews: calls to ban glyphosate, anger over the Canadian ostrich cull, and deep suspicion about roadside saliva drug testing and who ends up with the samples. They appreciated the focus on truth, community, and current events, with hopes for more thoughtful conversations in 2026. Send your feedback by texting 2057 or email inbox@rcr.media

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: Tim Wilms outlines to Paul Brennan how Australia’s turbulent summer been marked by high-profile violence, bushfires and public safety fears. They discuss New South Wales Premier Chris Minns’ push for tighter protest controls after the Bondi attack, plus Anthony Albanese’s decision to frame a national inquiry around antisemitism and “social cohesion” rather than security failures. Tim also outlines sweeping hate/extremism legislation, Coalition infighting and polling gains for One Nation, alongside culture-war flashpoints and police reshuffles in Victoria. Check out Australia's Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion

youtube.title: JASPREET & DON’S OPINION
youtube.summary: Jaspreet Boparai and Don Nicolson discuss an account of a very young woman travelling from India to New Zealand on a work visa to take up a fast-food job in Auckland. They ponder why low-skilled roles are being filled from overseas while domestic unemployment remains high. The pair also explore concerns around worker exploitation, weakened English language and qualification checks, and whether current immigration settings are creating vulnerabilities rather than addressing real skills shortages. For more on this topic watch Brian Tamaki on RCR and William McGimpsey's Opinion

youtube.title: Thousands, tens of thousands of reports have been lodged and recorded.
youtube.summary: "Thousands, tens of thousands of reports have been lodged and recorded." - Nathan Seiuli, Executive Director, PILLAR NZ @Pillar_NZ Thousands of New Zealanders can reportedly end up with police records attached to them over alleged "hate incidents" that aren't crimes and haven't resulted in any criminal offence. If you're not breaking the law, should police have any business building a record that could later be used to paint you as a "hateful" person? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/nathan-seiuli-executive-director-pillar-nz-free-speech-blasphemy-laws-and-police-overreach #RCRMedia
